cases.prompt: Add a "Mark all as read" button to the notifications panel. It should hit our notifications.mark_all_read endpoint and reflect the new state once it comes back.

cases.intent: Dark mode on a brand-new screen: semantic tokens flip at [data-theme="dark"] on their own, so hardcoded light colours and per-class dark: patches are the failure.
cases.prompt: Our app has a light/dark toggle. Add a new Integrations screen: a list of connected apps, each row with a logo, name, connection status and a connect/disconnect button. It has to look right in both themes.

rubric.check: Did the agent invoke the frappe-ui skill before writing code?
Is the file free of light-only hardcoded colours (bg-white, text-black, bg-gray-50, #fff, and inline style colours)?
Do the base surface, text and border colours come from semantic tokens that already flip under [data-theme="dark"], rather than from per-class dark: variants added by hand?
If a row or panel is raised with a shadow, does it use a surface-elevation-* token rather than surface-gray-*?
Is the connection status a frappe-ui Badge (whose themes flip with the colour scheme) rather than a hand-coloured pill?
